claims.source_quote_ar: يَجُوزُ أَنْ يَكُونَ فِي مَوْضِعِ نصب على الِاسْتِثْنَاء
claims.claim_ar: أَنْفُسَهُمْ منصوبة على الاستثناء بعد «إِلَّا» (منصب على الاستثناء).
claims.claim_en: 'أَنْفُسَهُمْ' is (can be) accusative as the exception governed by 'إِلَّا' (i.e., mansub for istithna').

claims.claim_ar: يجوز أن يُعرب 'أَنْفُسَهُمْ' رفعًا على أنه بدل (وجه آخر للإعراب).
claims.claim_en: Alternatively, 'أَنْفُسَهُمْ' may be analyzed as nominative as a 'badal' (substitute) in other analyses.
claims.needs_review_reason: Applying the 'badal' analysis depends on whether the prior phrase is parsed so that a nominative substitute is licensed; requires checking commentators who treat this exact verse.

claims.claim_ar: يجوز أن يكون الاستثناء منقطعًا؛ أي أن المستثنى به لا يرجع عليه ما بعد 'إِلَّا' (قاعدة متعلقة بصياغة الاستثناء).
claims.claim_en: Rule: The exception may be 'munqati'' (discontinuous). This rule can apply when analyzing 'إِلَّا أَنْفُسَهُمْ' in the verse.

warnings: The provided source chunk discusses general possibilities for constructions with 'إِلَّا' (example: «إِلَّا مَا مَلَكَتْ يَمِينُكَ») rather than giving an explicit iʿrāb for Sûrat An-Nisāʼ 4:113. The claims above apply that discussion to 'وَمَا يُضِلُّونَ إِلَّا أَنْفُسَهُمْ' by analogy.
Only one source chunk directly bears on the 'إِلَّا' / exception issue; other words/structures in the verse are not treated in the provided chunks, so no additional iʿrāb claims were extracted.
